q: 1. During the construction period, price variation clause in contracts caters to
options: increase in rates of only important materials
variation in cost in materials element, labour element and petrol-oil-lubricant element
variation in total cost of the project on an ad hoc basis
explain: The price variation clause adjusts for changes in the material, labour and POL cost components.

q: 2. Any event affecting the project should be claimed to client by the contractor within
explain: Standard international and local contracts (like FIDIC or PPR) typically require a notice of claim within 28 days of the event.

q: 3. The minimum number of parties for any types of dispute should be
explain: A dispute requires at least two opposing sides (e.g., the employer and the contractor).

q: 4. Which is the tri-party dispute resolution procedure for the settlement of any dispute in construction industry?
explain: Both DAB and Arbitration involve a third-party neutral body to settle disputes between the two contract parties.

q: 5. The number of members nominated in dispute adjudication board are
explain: A DAB typically consists of either a single member or three members to avoid deadlocks.

q: 6. The remuneration of members of dispute adjudication board is paid by
explain: Costs for the DAB are traditionally shared equally (50/50) by the contractor and the employer to maintain neutrality.

q: 7. The methods used for dispute resolution on any construction industry are
explain: All three methods are standard steps in the hierarchy of construction dispute resolution.

q: 8. During construction of governmental buildings the project became delayed due to delay in payment, unusual weather, civil disturbances etc. The reason, delay in payment will be considered for extra claim or not?
explain: A delay in payment by the employer is a breach of contract that allows the contractor to claim for time and/or cost.

q: 9. Mediation shall include the individuals directly involved in the dispute except
explain: Mediation focuses on direct party resolution; attorneys are often excluded or limited to allow for open dialogue.

q: 10. In the construction industry arbitration method is used for:
explain: Arbitration is a dispute resolution method used during contract execution, not related to tender inviting, opening, or awarding stages - hence none of the above.

q: 11. If the variation amount is in between 10% to15% of the original contract value then approval of the variation of cost is done by:
explain: For a variation of 10-15% of contract value, approval authority can rest with the project manager, site in-charge, or department head depending on the delegated authority level - so all of the above.

q: 12. In any project the works contracted with consultant and department. If drawings have been changed, how much authority of department head to give variation of ......percent of original contract amount in contract procedure? (Source:PPA2063(54))
explain: Under Public Procurement Act (PPA 2063, Section 54), the Department Head holds authority to approve variations up to 15% of the original contract price.

q: 13. The authority of Gazetted First Class to approve the variation amount upto-------of the original contract value. (Source: PPA2063(54))
explain: According to Section 54 of PPA 2063, a Gazetted First Class Officer (Project Chief/Chief Officer) can approve variations up to 10%.

q: 14. If the variation amount is more than 15% of the original contract value of sixty million, then approval of the variation of cost may be done by
explain: Variations exceeding standard threshold limits are escalated up to the Department Head or Council of Ministers as designated by PPA regulations.

q: 15. The department head can extend the time up to ……… % of initial contract duration.
explain: Per the answer key, 25%.

q: 16. Controlling the changes in the project may affect
explain: Change control impacts project progress, costs, and scope simultaneously - all of the above.

q: 17. Mediation shall include the individuals involved in the dispute except
explain: Mediation is an informal dispute resolution process between employer, contractor, and neutral mediator; formal legal representation (attorneys) is generally excluded.

q: 18. What a variation order may not necessarily contain?
explain: A variation order documents changes in quantities, rates, and new BOQ items, but does not necessarily specify overall project budget provisions.

q: 19. The final means of dispute resolution is
explain: Litigation (court proceedings) is generally regarded as the final/ultimate means of dispute resolution when other methods fail.

q: 20. Who issues variation order ?
explain: The project manager (on behalf of the client) is authorized to issue variation orders when changes to the scope are required.

q: 21. If variation occurs, what happens
explain: Variations can lead to increased costs and time, but occasionally a variation might decrease the scope and price.

q: 22. A variation order is issued to an contractor by the authorized personnel of the client when
options: it becomes necessary to change design and drawing
the quantity of items given in the contract document is to be charged
new items of work are required to be added
explain: Variations are used for any material change in the drawings, quantities, or scope of work defined in the original contract.

q: 23. In any project the works contracted with consultant and department. If drawings have been changed, how much authority of department head to give variation of ......percent of original contract amount in contract procedure?
explain: Under PPA 2063, the head of the department generally has the authority to approve variations up to 15% of the original cost.

q: 24. The authority of Gazatted First Class to approve the variation amount upto--------of the original contract value.
explain: Per specific PPA thresholds, a Gazetted First Class officer typically has authority for variations up to 10%.

q: 25. Due to alteration of any component of the project the cost of original contract value
explain: An alteration can result in an increase, a decrease, or (rarely) no net change to the total cost.

q: 26. Due to alteration of any component of the project the duration of project
explain: Changes to components often impact the schedule, potentially increasing or decreasing the total project time.

q: 27. Due to omission of any component of the project the cost of project
explain: Removing a component from the scope of work (omission) naturally leads to a reduction in the project cost.

q: 28. Due to omission of any component of the project the duration of project may be
explain: The answer key specifies 'constant', suggesting that in many contract scenarios, omitting a minor component might not shorten the overall contractual duration.

q: 29. Any variation to a contract should be
options: fully considered (including the impact and risk)
explain: Proper contract variation management requires full consideration of impact/risk, documentation, and formal approval - all of the above.
